Asobi Review 0.2 (build 501)

Color follows the grader — on every seat, including the web.

  • Grades follow live in hosted sessions. Adjust exposure, CDL or looks and every connected Asobi — internal or Review — re-applies the same grade in its own color pipeline, so an EXR seat and an optimized-media seat land on the same picture. Late joiners receive the room's grade on arrival. Look files travel with the grade; a look a seat can't be given is dropped there, never guessed at.
  • Web pages follow as a live trim — a small display-referred correction applied over their streamed video in WebGL, the way a DIT trims through a monitor path. Immediate and faithful in the mids; blind to highlights their proxy already clipped.
  • New: File ▸ Update Web Share with Current Grades re-renders shared clips with grades baked in — exact web pixels, minutes not milliseconds, and the page retires its live trim for those clips automatically so nothing applies twice.
  • The grade tools tell you about web viewers. Review Grade and Film Lab show a banner whenever web seats are connected: following approximately, not following (toggle off), or unable to follow — each with the remedy named.
  • All of it is switchable in Settings ▸ Color ▸ Color to Other Seats, and Settings itself has been redesigned — tinted section icons, clearer grouping, and footers that explain what each control actually does.
  • Fixed: exposure meant different things on different media. +1 EV on an optimized stand-in rendered 80/255 brighter than the same EV on the EXR. Exposure now applies in scene-linear whatever the media, which grade-follow made mandatory: a grade must be one picture on every seat.
  • The manual covers all of the above (expert chapters 5 and 10, client chapter 3).

Asobi Review 0.2 (build 494)

Print-film looks now apply the way Resolve applies them.

  • Film Lab looks apply after the display transform, on display-referred picture — the standard placement for a print emulation, and how a 2383 PFE sits in a Resolve node tree. Previously the look ran before the tonemap, in scene space, where everything above diffuse white fell outside the LUT's range: 2 stops over and 4 stops over both flattened to one value, below diffuse white. Measured now: highlights stay graded and monotonic at every strength — 2-over and 4-over land at distinct values with the print shoulder intact.
  • Strength blends cleanly at any setting. Halfway between no look and the full print, instead of blending against a clipped image.
  • Looks will render slightly differently than before — denser, more print-like in the mids, with highlights that keep their gradation. That is the placement change doing its job; recipes and saved looks are unchanged and re-render through the new placement automatically. Look chips re-render to match.
  • This applies to Film Lab looks — live and saved ones (recognized by the recipe file saved beside the cube). Library LUTs that declare their own working spaces (camera-log print LUTs and the like) are already in their right place and are untouched.

Asobi Review 0.2 (build 493)

A look at 0% is exactly no look, and look chips take the click.

  • Fixed: turning a look down to 0% still rolled off the whites. A look at reduced strength is baked into a lattice blended toward identity — but a lattice is only identity inside the 0–1 range of its working space, and log material carries plenty of picture above that. Everything over range clamped at the lattice edge: measured, a 2-stop-over value displayed 9% dark and a 4-stop-over value 14% dark, both flattened to the same ceiling — with the look at zero. A layer at 0% is now dropped from the chain entirely, verified pixel-identical to no look at all.
  • Verified both color modes while in there: the same Film Lab look renders the same on a native EXR and on its ACEScct optimized stand-in — channel means agree within 0.2%, with the remaining difference being 4K-vs-HD detail, not color.
  • Fixed: look chips ignoring clicks. Each chip's thumbnail spills invisibly outside its pill, and that spill was a live click region sitting on top of the neighboring chips — so clicks landed on a neighbor's invisible overflow instead of the chip under the cursor. The click target is now exactly the pill.
  • Worth knowing: at strengths above 0%, a print-film look still compresses values above diffuse white — that is what a display-referred print emulation does. If a look should leave super-whites alone, that is a pipeline-placement change worth discussing, not a slider fix.
